posts.title: Toll rises to 469 as police publish new district count
body: Nepal Police put the confirmed toll at 469 dead as of a 7am bulletin on Friday, up from 389 at 9pm Thursday and 359 at 5pm. Police also said 466 people are injured, a figure not revised since Thursday. The flood hit Timure in Rasuwa on Wednesday morning and ran down the Bhote Koshi into the Trishuli and the Narayani.

Friday's bulletin also gave a new district breakdown that for the first time adds up to the full 469: Chitwan 178, Nawalparasi East 110, Gorkha 44, Nuwakot 37, Dhading 33, Tanahun 28, Nawalparasi West 27 and Rasuwa 12. Health facilities in Chitwan, which has the most bodies, can hold only around 50 at a time, which is slowing identification and release to families.

NDRRMA's 6:20pm update on Thursday listed 910 people out of contact in Nepal, up from 826 that morning, 570 of them tourists. Nepal's tourism board says 517 of the missing are foreign nationals, from 33 countries. Out of contact does not mean dead. Phone lines, power and internet are down across the valley and are coming back slowly.

China's Ministry of Water Resources says a new barrier lake near the Chhochen Khola and Purepu Tsangpo, close to the Nepal border, is already overflowing and holds about 2 million cubic metres of water. It expects another 3 million cubic metres to flow in over three days from Thursday, putting the lake at high risk of breaching in that time. This is separate from the smaller lake NDRRMA found earlier on the Lhende river. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV says 555 tourists and nearly 500 local residents have been evacuated from the Tibet side near the border, ABC News reports.

USGS first read the shaking on Wednesday as an earthquake. It later found no earthquake took place. The signal came from an ice and rock avalanche that fell into the Lhende Khola on the Tibet side, dammed the river, then broke.

Nepal's Army says more than 5,000 army and police personnel are working the flood zone, from Nuwakot to Chitwan. Prime Minister Balendra Shah travelled to Bidur in Nuwakot on Thursday to see the damage.

In India, the NDRF and the Sashastra Seema Bal have rescue teams on standby in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, and the NDRF says the Gandak, which the Narayani becomes downstream, could see higher water levels. Nepal has turned down offers of search and rescue teams from India, China, the US, Britain, Japan, South Korea, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, the Kathmandu Post reports. The government says its own army and police can handle the operation and is asking instead for cash, through a single channel into the Prime Minister's Disaster Relief Fund.
Keep off the banks of the Bhote Koshi, the Trishuli and the Narayani until officials say it is clear.

posts.title: Damage put at Rs 200 billion, hydropower losses still being counted
body: Physical Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal said damage to roads and bridges is around Rs 200 billion. He called it preliminary information.

That figure does not include energy infrastructure. Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha has ordered an immediate assessment of hydropower damage. In Rasuwa, 8 projects have been hit, 5 of them operational with a combined 236 megawatts, and 3 still under construction with a combined 342 megawatts. Nuwakot has lost access to 6 more projects, 4 operational at 123 megawatts and 2 under construction at 53 megawatts.
Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan are still being surveyed for road and building damage, so the Rs 200 billion figure is expected to rise.

The government has released Rs 1 billion to the disaster relief fund, plus Rs 10 million each to Rasuwa and Nuwakot and Rs 5 million to Dhading. The World Bank has separately offered up to Rs 25 billion in emergency assistance, its Nepal country director told the finance ministry. That is aid, not a damage estimate.
Insurers say claims will take weeks to settle because most of the damaged sites cannot be reached by road.

The Prime Minister's Disaster Relief Fund took in Rs 273.3 million in donations in its first six hours, the finance ministry says, led by a Rs 100 million gift from Gorkha Brewery. That is public donations, separate from the Rs 1 billion the government has already released for relief.

UNICEF says at least 17,000 children have been affected across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. It counts 18 schools destroyed and 20 more damaged in those three districts, wider than the 8 schools Onlinekhabar had reported damaged in Rasuwa and Nuwakot alone a day earlier. UNICEF says around 10,000 school-age children now need help such as temporary classrooms and replacement books to keep learning.

posts.title: Army pulls 350 from Upper Trishuli tunnel, more still inside
body: The Nepali Army has pulled more than 350 workers and local villagers out of a flooded access tunnel at the under construction Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, rescuers rappelling from a hovering helicopter to reach the entrance, Bloomberg reports, citing Nepal's Prime Minister's Office. More than 100 people were still believed trapped inside as of Thursday, and the operation is continuing.

The Nepali Army said separately that its units have rescued more than 300 people across the flood zone so far, spokesperson Brigadier General Raja Ram Basnet said, a wider tally than NDRRMA's earlier, named count of 113. It is not confirmed how these counts relate to each other. Around two dozen helicopters and nearly 1,000 personnel from the Nepal Police, Nepali Army and Armed Police Force are working the search, the Kathmandu Post reports.

At Trishuli 3A in Mailung, where 35 workers were reported cut off on Wednesday with the tunnel gate blocked, the army airlifted three people out on Thursday, Onlinekhabar reports. It has not said how many remain inside.

At the Langtang Hydropower project, more than 25 workers have been out of contact in a tunnel since Wednesday. Bijay Mohan Bhattarai, the company's managing director and a secretary of IPPAN, said government agencies need to step up rescue efforts there, and that all available helicopters had already been sent elsewhere, Onlinekhabar reports.

The Independent Power Producers' Association Nepal, IPPAN, says 215 staff from five hydropower projects in total have not been reached since Wednesday's flood. Worst hit is Upper Trishuli-1 itself, with 94 people out of contact by IPPAN's count, a narrower figure than the more than 350 the army says it has now brought out of that project's tunnel. At Rasuwagadhi, 51 staff are out of contact, though 3 reached higher ground on their own.

posts.title: Australia raises its missing count to 39, pledges $5m in aid
body: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong said on Friday that 39 Australians are now unaccounted for in the flood, up from the 35 that Nepal's tourism board had listed a day earlier. She said the number could still rise as officials work through the list, and warned some of those missing may not be found.

Wong also announced A$5 million in Australian aid: 2 million to the World Food Programme, 2 million to Australian NGOs through the Australian Humanitarian Partnership, and 1 million to the Emergency Action Alliance for local recovery work. Three more Australian humanitarian specialists are being sent to join the 20 staff already in Nepal.

posts.title: Rasuwa still cut off, thousands sheltering with almost nothing
body: Rasuwa remains cut off from the rest of Nepal two days after the flood, with roads, power and phone lines still down in the worst hit areas, Onlinekhabar reports.

About 3,500 people are sheltering in Uttargaya rural municipality alone, including students, displaced families, elderly people, pregnant women and people who need oxygen, local officials told Onlinekhabar.

Uttargaya chair Madhav Aryal said the municipality now has two ambulances and one vehicle left. "The minimum responsibility that the state should fulfil has not been met," he said. Gosainkunda chair Kaisang Nurpu Tamang described what supplies remain there in two words: "Nothing, nothing."

Around 150 people who fled a hydropower project are stranded across a river with no way to reach food, and 36 students are separated from their families in Nuwakot because access routes are damaged, Onlinekhabar reports.
Local officials in Uttargaya believe as many as 750 people from the municipality may still be missing. That figure is their own estimate and has not been confirmed by police or NDRRMA.

People trying to get aid into Rasuwa should coordinate through the district disaster relief committee or the army rather than travelling in on their own. Most access roads into the district are still down.

posts.title: Universities told to postpone exams from Friday because of the floods
body: Education and Sports Minister Sasmit Pokharel has directed university vice-chancellors to postpone all examinations scheduled from 29 August because of the floods, Onlinekhabar reports.
Universities are also told to suspend non-essential gatherings, workshops and seminars, and to arrange re-examinations for students who could not sit exams on 28 August.
The ministry said the order is meant to protect students, parents, teachers and staff while the disaster response continues.

posts.title: Prithvi Highway still blocked, reopening targeted for Friday
body: The Prithvi Highway, the main road between Kathmandu and Pokhara, has been blocked since Wednesday evening after Bhotekoshi floodwater dumped mud across it in Gajuri and Galchhi, in Dhading, Onlinekhabar reports.

Debris still has to be cleared at three sites: Galoudi and Bahuni Bhir in Gajuri, and Mahesh Dobhan in Galchhi. Traffic police superintendent Dilli Narayan Pandey said clearing near settlements is what is causing the delay.
Authorities are aiming to reopen the highway by the end of Friday.
